description.text: The path drops away from your door in a series of worn turns, chalk showing through the grass where generations of feet have cut the corner. Below, Hollowbrook is a scatter of dark roofs and one lit window, and the mill wheel has stopped for the night.

The path drops away from your door in a series of worn turns, and the whole village lies below in the early light — chimney smoke going straight up, the mill wheel turning, somebody's dog answering somebody else's.

The path drops away from your door in a series of worn turns, chalk showing through the grass where generations of feet have cut the corner. Hollowbrook sits below in the crook of its brook: the square, the mill, lanes running off east and west between low thatched roofs.

skills.text: Stop and look out over the village
resultText: From up here the whole shape of it is plain: every lane bends toward the well, and every roof turns its back to the ridge. Somebody laid this village out on purpose, a long time ago, and nobody since has needed to change it.

You pick out the museum's roofline behind you, higher than anything below. From the village, your family's house is the first thing you'd see coming up the valley — and the easiest thing to stop noticing.
Twenty-odd chimneys, and you find yourself counting them. Seventy-some people down there, give or take a baby, and until this week you could not have named four.
